rows.grounds: those to whom the practitioner becomes dear

items.question: What attainments make a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment is named as an attainment.
Liberation is named as an attainment.
Great accomplishment is named as an attainment.
Possessing these makes one dear to the yoginīs.
items.inference: A practitioner who attains enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: One may become dear to the yoginīs through enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment.

The emergence is located in Candra-dvīpa.
items.inference: The ninth chapter emerges in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter, emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

rows.grounds: describes the state of the self
describes the posture of the self

items.question: In what posture and condition is the self to be visualized or understood?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire.
The self stands on one foot.
Both condition and posture describe the same self.
items.inference: The self is to be conceived as surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
uncertainties: Whether this is a visualization instruction or a descriptive statement is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

rows.grounds: what is requested to be made manifest

items.question: What revelation about knowledge is being requested from the deity?
premises: The speaker addresses the god.
The speaker requests manifestation today.
The object requested is the determination of knowledge.
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to make manifest the determination of knowledge.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

manner or extent of knowing fully

items.question: What structured division of octads does the speaker seek to know fully?
premises: A division of eight octads is named.
The speaker seeks to know it fully.
The knowing is described as endless or complete.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and completely the division of the eight octads.
uncertainties: The precise sense of anantathā as endlessly or in infinite detail is interpretive.
items.plain_english: And to know fully and completely the division of the eight octads.

rows.grounds: spiritual center or diagram in question

items.question: How can the secret place or wheel be quickly accomplished according to Bhairava?
premises: A secret place is mentioned.
A wheel is mentioned as being accomplished.
Quick accomplishment is the desired manner.
items.inference: The speaker asks Bhairava how the secret place and wheel can be quickly accomplished.
uncertainties: Whether guhya sthānaṃ and cakraṃ are distinct or appositional is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell me how the secret place and the wheel are quickly accomplished.

rows.grounds: first member indicating rarity among gods

items.question: How does Bhairava evaluate the question asked by the great goddess?
premises: Bhairava expresses approval twice.
Bhairava states he has been asked.
The matter asked about is hard to obtain even for gods.
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess's question as concerning something rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

rows.grounds: location or identity assigned to kṣa
seed syllable located in the forehead

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the brahmarandhra and the forehead?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead.
Each syllable is given a specific bodily locus.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

seed syllable located in the heart

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the throat region and the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is placed in the heart.

items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

object the listener is asked to hear

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
Their meditation is now offered as teaching.
The beloved is asked to listen.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus associated with the first octad described?
premises: The lotus is divine.
The lotus has eight spokes.
The lotus is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Meditate on the divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: means by which steadiness is gained
first member of social duty compound

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with a mind steadied by practice adopt?
premises: Practice leads to an even mind.
Village or conventional duty is named.

items.inference: Through practice, one with an even mind should abandon conventional village duties.
uncertainties: grāma-dharma may refer broadly to conventional social obligations.
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an even mind, one should abandon the duties of ordinary village life.

rows.grounds: first member of the knowledge compound
siddhi of arresting bonds or forces

items.question: What specific powers arise in this stage of practice for the beloved?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is named.
Paralysis of bonds is named.
Both are presented as attained results.
items.inference: This practice yields the powers of distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobha can mean arresting bonds or immobilizing hostile forces.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly stated for the goddess in this context?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment.
Transformation is named as an attainment.
These are stated in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the practice also yields immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: The exact nature of parivartanam as transformation or reversal is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: O goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and likewise transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second lotus is identified.
It has eight petals.
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second lotus is eight-petaled and brightly illuminated through fire meditation.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What power arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
The practitioner makes form.
The form is made in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

unmoving beings included in the world

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner is described as angry.
The action is destruction or withdrawal.
The object is the entire triple world with moving and unmoving beings.
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world, both moving and unmoving.
uncertainties: saṃharet may mean withdraw or dissolve rather than destroy in a literal sense.
items.plain_english: When angered, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is named.
Seeing from very far away is named.

items.inference: The practice removes wrinkles and grey hair and grants vision from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: What disciplined practice in solitude enables the creation of many forms?
premises: The practitioner is in solitude.
The practitioner is intent on meditation.
The practitioner is instructed to make many forms.
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, the practitioner should create many forms.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation between making form and performing meditation is compressed.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice.
Immortality is named as the result.
The result is asserted emphatically.
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What happens to age-related death through abstention from eating by day?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified.
Age-related death is named.
A future departure or overcoming is stated.
items.inference: Through abstention from eating by day, age-related death will be overcome.
uncertainties: The exact sense of gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ is interpretive; it may mean death will depart.
items.plain_english: By not eating during the day, one will overcome death from old age.

rows.grounds: means by which the result occurs

items.question: What bodily form results from constant practice of this yoga?
premises: Constant practice yoga is the means.

This form becomes the practitioner's state.
items.inference: Through constant practice of this yoga, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ is interpreted as the appearance of sixteen years.
items.plain_english: Through constant practice of this yoga, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What contemplative visualization grants the power to shake the triple world?
premises: A smoke-colored object or hue is to be contemplated.
The contemplation is to be done always.
The result is shaking the triple world.
items.inference: By always contemplating the smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
uncertainties: The object that is smoke-colored is not explicitly named in this verse.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating what is smoke-colored, one can shake the triple world.
